decisions.reason: ACE3 was publicly launched as the new industry standard for the firm's core airfield lighting control business, so the sunk investment, its centrality and the visible commitment all argue for keeping it despite limited recent visibility.
The airport systems training program supports the firm's service and installed-base strategy, needs little investment, and weak results can be blamed on pandemic disruption to airport traffic.

The airfield ground lighting course ties directly to the firm's core lighting business and its customer support, so dropping it would undercut the established offer, and slow uptake can be attributed to the temporary pandemic downturn.

The collaboration software embodies the announced move toward collaborative decision-making and integrated operations, so management would justify continuing it and treat weak demand as a temporary effect of COVID.

The MLAT system was announced as a flagship at inter airport Europe and is central to the firm's surveillance and integration direction, so the public commitment and invested R&D strongly favor persisting with it.
